1.title: Managing Product Delivery in Context
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Managing Product Delivery in Context. It covers the exam area The prince two processes. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. four point five.one apply managing product delivery: activities, inputs and outputs, roles and responsibilities, how the practices are applied. four point five.two analyze whether the activities, roles and responsibilities are effective and fit for purpose, considering tailoring, the practices, and the purpose and objectives of the process. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two processes (thirty percent). Exam format: an open-book scenario exam: one hundred fifty minutes, seventy marks, forty-two marks to pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Practitioner syllabus (people cert), version seven point two.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves
1.text: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves. Managing product delivery is the team manager's process. It is the formal link between the project manager and the team manager. The figure shows the three activities.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves, continued
1.text: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves. The figure shows this: Managing product delivery: the team manager accepts a work package, executes it with checkpoint reports and delivers the completed products to the project manager.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves, continued
1.text: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves. Purpose: control the link between the project manager and the team manager by placing formal requirements on accepting, executing and delivering project work. Objectives: work on products is authorized and agreed; the team knows what is expected, including effort, cost and time; products are delivered to the expected quality and within tolerance; progress information reaches the project manager at an agreed frequency.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves, continued
1.text: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves. Focus on products. The work package asks for defined products with quality criteria. Manage by exception. The work package has tolerances; a forecast breach goes to the project manager. Define roles, responsibilities and relationships. Team managers report to the project manager, not to the board. Continued business justification. Unapproved extras that add cost are not delivered. Learn from experience. Lessons from the work are passed on. Exam tip: The team manager agrees the work package before accepting it, including the tolerances. An option where the team starts without agreement, or ignores the tolerances, is a red flag.

1.title: Activities, inputs and outputs
1.text: Activities, inputs and outputs. The names below give the general idea; check the Official Book's wording for the activities. Accept a work package. Reviews the work package description; agrees products, tolerances, quality and reporting; plans the work, with a team plan if needed. Execute a work package. Builds the products; applies the quality method; sends checkpoint reports; raises issues and risks. Deliver a work package. Gets products approved, hands them over as agreed and tells the project manager the work is complete.

1.title: Activities, inputs and outputs, continued
1.text: Activities, inputs and outputs. Inputs. The authorized work package: work package description, product descriptions, tolerances, constraints, reporting needs. Outputs. Checkpoint reports; the team plan; quality records; completed products with approvals; issues, risks and lessons raised to the project manager. Exam tip: Team managers report to the project manager, not to the board. The board hears about the stage through the highlight report, which the project manager writes.

1.title: Roles
1.text: Roles. Team manager. Responsible: accepts, executes and delivers the work package; agrees tolerances; reports. Project manager. Authorizes and agrees the work package; receives reports and products; keeps control. Team members. Do the work to the quality asked. Senior supplier. Makes supplier resources available; is accountable for supplier quality. Senior user. Provides users for reviews and approvals when needed. Project assurance. Checks quality and progress independently. Change authority. Decides changes that the project manager brings as issues. Project support. Keeps product status and configuration records. Check the book's roles table for this process. The general rule: the project manager authorizes and the team manager delivers.

1.title: How the practices are applied
1.text: How the practices are applied. Quality. Product descriptions guide the work; quality methods are applied; quality records and approvals are kept. Plans. The team plan fits the work package and its tolerances. Risk. The team manager reports risks and manages those delegated. Issues. Changes, problems and concerns go to the project manager; the team does not approve changes. Progress. Checkpoint reports at the agreed frequency; early warning of a tolerance breach. Organization. Reporting lines are clear, including supplier teams under the commercial management approach. Business case. Deliver what is needed for the benefits; no extras.

1.title: Judging a scenario
1.text: Judging a scenario. The team manager agrees the work package, including tolerances, and negotiates if it is unrealistic. Accepting an unrealistic work package silently, or starting before agreeing it. Checkpoint reports at the agreed frequency show status, forecast, issues and risks. No reports until the work is done. Quality records show products were checked against the product description and approved. Delivery with no evidence of checks.

1.title: Judging a scenario, continued
1.text: Judging a scenario. Changes are raised to the project manager as issues. Unapproved changes or extra features inside the work package. A forecast breach of the work package tolerance is raised at once. Carrying on and hoping to catch up. Completion is confirmed to the project manager and products are handed over as agreed. Products passed straight to users or the board.

1.title: Judging a scenario, continued
1.text: Judging a scenario. Tailoring changes the form, not the agreement. Supplier teams: the work package matches the contract and the commercial management approach. The supplier keeps its own methods and reports in an agreed format. Agile delivery: the team uses its own iterations and backlog. The work package states the products, priorities and tolerances (often fixed time and cost, flexible scope), and team data can serve as checkpoint information. Small projects: the project manager may also be the team manager. The agreement is lighter, but what, when and how much are still clear.

2.title: Judging a scenario, continued
2.text: Judging a scenario. Sustainability, digital and data: the work package can state sustainability or data protection needs for the products. Exam tip: A team can use its own method but must still agree the work package, report to the project manager and meet the quality asked. A supplier is not exempt from the process.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Wei Chen's team receives a work package to build the berth-permit form in four weeks. Wei knows the team has only half the staff needed, but starts work without comment, hoping to catch up. Was this an appropriate action for the team manager to take, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: No, because the work package must be agreed as achievable before starting. Accepting a work package means agreeing that the products, effort and tolerances are achievable, and an unrealistic one must be raised with the project manager first.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. The harbor master mentions an extra online payment feature, and Wei Chen's team adds it to the work package without telling the project manager. Was this an appropriate action for the team manager to take, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: No, because changes must go to the project manager as an issue. Changes are handled through the issues practice, so the team manager raises it with the project manager and the change authority decides.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Halfway through a work package, Wei Chen's team forecasts that it will exceed the agreed time tolerance by three days. The next weekly checkpoint report is in five days. What should Wei do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Tell the project manager at once so that action can be agreed. A forecast breach of work package tolerance is escalated promptly to the project manager (manage by exception), not held for the next report.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Delta Software's team has finished a work package and every product was checked. Who is responsible for telling the project manager that the work package is complete and for handing the products over? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Wei Chen, the team manager. The team manager delivers the work package and confirms completion to the project manager.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Sam Okafor and Wei Chen agree that Wei will report on the progress of a work package each week, with forecasts and issues. Which management product does Wei send? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Checkpoint report. The checkpoint report goes from the team manager to the project manager at the agreed frequency.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Delta Software's team uses its own sprint method. Wei Chen agrees the products, tolerances and weekly checkpoint information with Sam Okafor, and the team plans its own sprints. Was this appropriate tailoring, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Yes, because the work package is agreed and the team keeps its method. The work package, tolerances and reporting are agreed, which is what the process requires, while the method is the team's choice.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the purpose of managing product delivery? Answer: To control the link between the project manager and the team manager with formal requirements for accepting, executing and delivering work. Question two. Whose process is managing product delivery? Answer: The team manager's. Question three. Name the three activities. Answer: Accept a work package, execute a work package and deliver a work package.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which report does the team manager send to the project manager during execution? Answer: The checkpoint report. Question five. What should the team manager do with a change that comes up inside a work package? Answer: Raise it with the project manager as an issue. Question six. What shows that products were checked before delivery? Answer: Quality records, with the approvals.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Purpose: formal link between project manager and team manager: accept, execute, deliver. Activities: accept, execute and deliver a work package. Inputs: the authorized work package with product descriptions and tolerances. Outputs: checkpoint reports, team plan, quality records, completed products. Roles: team manager responsible; project manager authorizes and receives. Effective: agreed work package, checkpoints, quality records, no unapproved changes. Red flags: silent acceptance, hidden slippage, extras, reporting to the board. Tailoring: supplier and agile teams keep their method but still agree and report.
